metadata.case_name: MARLENE SUSANNE COURBET v. MANDARIN DIVERS MARINE SERVICES LTD. AND OTHERS

source: Dr Choa diagnosed her as suffering from post-concussional syndrome and treated her accordingly.

injuries.description: damage to the greater occipital nerve (GON)
source: Both agree that some of the headaches are the result of damage to the greater occipital nerve (GON) occasioned by the accident

injuries.description: trauma to an already degenerated spine (cervical spine) occasioning persistent headaches
source: another type of more persistent headache occasioned by trauma to an already degenerated spine.
X-rays taken of her spine on the date of the accident showed in particular wide-spread degenerative change in the cervical spine especially from C 3 to C 7 level.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the neck

manifestations.description: headaches (starting at the back of her head and tending to spread over the left side)
persistent headaches occasioned by trauma to an already degenerated spine
pain over neck, shoulders and upper back
dizziness and nausea / vomiting immediately after the accident
depression and anxiety attacks (mental symptoms over two years, now subsided)
difficulty in concentrating and absorbing material; affects attention and concentration at work
sensitivity to noise and crowds (could not stand noise or crowds)

treatments_received: Treated and discharged from the Accident Emergency Department at Tang Shiu Kin Hospital
Consultation and treatment by Dr Brian Choa for post-concussional syndrome

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Sporting activities considerably curtailed as a result of the accident: tennis shortened and played less frequently, only plays low-grade hockey less often, unable to swim, vigorous gym work triggers headaches.
Being single her social life centred around her sporting activities which have been considerably curtailed as a result of the accident.

losses.category: Loss of ability to enjoy quiet or solitude
losses.description: Could not stand noise or crowds; sensitivity to noise affects her ability to cope and concentration.
